variables.title: Variables
variables.code:
set name "Fish User"
set -l local_var "local"
set -g global_var "global"
variables.notes: Fish does not use `=` for assignment, it uses the `set` command.

data_types.title: Data Types
data_types.notes: Fish uses lists (arrays) natively; variables are fundamentally lists of strings.

operators.title: Operators
operators.notes: Fish uses the `math` command instead of expr or `(())`.

conditionals.title: Conditionals
conditionals.code:
if test $a -gt $b
  echo "Greater"
else if test $a -eq $b
  echo "Equal"
else
  echo "Less"
end

while_loop.title: While Loop
while_loop.code:
while test $i -lt 5
  echo $i
  set i (math $i + 1)
end

functions.title: Functions
functions.code:
function greet
  set name $argv[1]
  echo "Hello $name"
end
functions.notes: Uses `$argv` instead of `$1` (though `$1` may work). No `{}`.

maps.title: Maps
maps.code:
# Simulating with parallel lists
set keys key1 key2
set vals val1 val2

error_handling.title: Error Handling
error_handling.notes: Uses `and`/`or` instead of `&&`/`||` in older versions (though newer fish supports them).

comments.title: Comments & Annotations
comments.code:
-- Single-line comment
{- Multi-line
   comment block -}
add :: Int -> Int -> Int
add a b = a + b
comments.notes: Idris uses functional comment delimiters (-- in Haskell/ML, ; in Lisps, # or % in BEAM).

numbers.title: Numbers & Numerics
numbers.code:
x = 42 :: Int
big = 100000000000000000000 :: Integer
piVal = 3.14159 :: Double
hexVal = 0xFF
numbers.notes: Idris supports exact rational fractions, arbitrary-precision integers, and IEEE floats natively.

booleans.title: Booleans & Logic
booleans.code:
isActive = True
isDone = False
result = isActive && not isDone
booleans.notes: Idris treats booleans as first-class algebraic constructors (True/False, true/false, t/nil).

type_casting.title: Type Conversion
type_casting.code:
intVal = 42 :: Int
floatVal = fromIntegral intVal :: Double
strVal = show intVal
parsed = read "123" :: Int
type_casting.notes: Idris performs conversion via typeclass methods (fromIntegral, show, read) or explicit parse functions.

strings.title: Strings & Text
strings.notes: Idris represents strings as linked lists of characters, UTF-8 binaries, or dedicated text buffers.

string_formatting.title: String Formatting
string_formatting.code:
import Text.Printf
msg = printf "User %s scored %d" "Alice" (95 :: Int)
string_formatting.notes: Idris formats text through format strings, interpolation macros, or string concatenation.

pattern_matching.title: Pattern Matching
pattern_matching.code:
describeList xs = case xs of
    []       -> "Empty list"
    [x]      -> "Single element"
    (x:y:_)  -> "Multiple elements"
pattern_matching.notes: Pattern matching is a core feature in Idris, destructuring algebraic variants, tuples, and lists directly.

range.title: Ranges & Sequences
range.code:
-- Infinite lazy sequence
evens = [0, 2 .. 20]
-- List slice with take/drop
sub = take 5 (drop 2 [1..10])
range.notes: Idris constructs ranges as lazy lists, infinite streams, or structured range enumerables.

iterators.title: Iterators & Comprehensions
iterators.code:
-- List comprehension
squares = [x * x | x <- [1..10], even x]
iterators.notes: Idris achieves iterative processing through list comprehensions, map/filter transforms, and recursion.

oop_classes.title: Types & Abstractions (OOP Equivalent)
oop_classes.notes: Idris emphasizes algebraic data types, protocols/typeclasses, and structs over traditional class hierarchies.

lists.title: Lists (Linked Lists)
lists.code:
list = [1, 2, 3]
appended = 0 : list  -- Cons: O(1)
merged = list ++ [4, 5] -- Concat
lists.notes: Lists in Idris are singly linked immutable sequences optimized for head/tail structural sharing.

tuples.title: Tuples & Records
tuples.notes: Idris uses fixed-length heterogeneous tuples for bundling related data points and function return values.

sets.title: Sets
sets.code:
import qualified Data.Set as Set
s = Set.fromList [1, 2, 3]
s' = Set.insert 4 s
exists = Set.member 2 s'
sets.notes: Idris provides persistent immutable sets implemented via balanced binary trees (HAMT / AVL).

modules_import.title: Modules & Imports
modules_import.notes: Idris isolates scopes through modules and explicit import lists with aliasing and qualified names.
